welcome: Ready, world traveler? Spin the globe and see where our story lands!
drag-help: Swipe the globe, or tap the big spin button.
closer: You’re getting close. Follow the glowing pin.
landed: We found it! Tap the glowing pin to open the storybook.
passport-open: Here is your world passport. Every place you visit gets a stamp.
page-complete: You discovered the whole page. Stamp your passport!
all-complete: Five wonderful places! Our big world is full of animals, homes, and stories.
replay: Let’s spin around the world again.
prompt-asia: Spin to Asia, the biggest continent.
landing-asia: Welcome to Asia. Let’s open a bamboo forest story.
asia-animal: Giant pandas use strong jaws to munch crunchy bamboo.
asia-habitat: Bamboo forests give pandas food, shade, and places to climb.
asia-wonder: A panda can spend much of its day eating bamboo.
prompt-africa: Spin to Africa, where the savanna stretches wide.
landing-africa: Welcome to Africa. Let’s open a sunny savanna story.
africa-animal: African elephants use their trunks to breathe, drink, and pick things up.
africa-habitat: Savannas are wide grasslands with scattered trees.
africa-wonder: Elephant families travel together and help care for their calves.
prompt-australia: Spin to Australia, a continent surrounded by ocean.
landing-australia: Welcome to Australia. Let’s open a eucalyptus woodland story.
australia-animal: Koalas grip branches with strong paws and sharp claws.
australia-habitat: Eucalyptus trees give koalas both food and a place to rest.
australia-wonder: Koalas sleep for many hours so their bodies can save energy.
prompt-north-america: Spin to North America, between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
landing-north-america: Welcome to North America. Let’s open a mountain forest story.
north-america-animal: Brown bears have an excellent sense of smell.
north-america-habitat: Mountain forests can offer bears berries, roots, rivers, and shelter.
north-america-wonder: Many brown bears rest in dens through the coldest part of winter.
prompt-south-america: Spin to South America, home to the great Amazon rainforest.
landing-south-america: Welcome to South America. Let’s open a rainforest story.
south-america-animal: A toucan uses its long, light beak to reach fruit on slender branches.
south-america-habitat: Rainforests are warm, wet, and layered with plant life.
south-america-wonder: Toucans toss fruit into the air and catch it in their beaks.
